inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares (390.1M, quarter ended 2026-06-30), after $603.6M of H1-2026 buybacks. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The 0.375% convertible notes due 2028 convert far above the current price, so they are treated as debt at face, not as dilution.
inputs.debt_detail: XBRL TotalDebt mapped to nothing; read from the SEC companyfacts API instead. 2026-06-30: 0.375% convertible senior notes due 2028 at $1,250.0M face (carrying $1,242.8M, tag ConvertibleLongTermNotesPayable) + finance-lease liabilities ~$59.0M ($52.3M non-current at 2026-06-30 + $6.7M current at 2025-12-31, the latest current figure tagged). The $1.2B 0.25% notes due 2025 were settled in Q4 2025 (ConvertibleNotesPayableCurrent $1,206.9M at 2025-09-30 -> $0 at 2025-12-31; cash + securities fell by a matching amount). Revolver undrawn apart from ~$8.7M of letters of credit.
inputs.cash_detail: Cash and equivalents $1,105.0M + current available-for-sale debt securities $704.8M + non-current available-for-sale debt securities $137.2M, all at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q). Strategic long-term investments ($209.5M) are carried separately in equity_bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back (ShareBasedCompensation $159.6M). FY2025 tax withholding on net-share settlement was not tagged and was $0 through H1-2025 (sell-to-cover); from 2026 DexCom net-settles ($37.6M in H1-2026), so the forward SBC path starts at ~3.9% of revenue = TTM SBC $162.4M + $37.6M withholding over TTM revenue $4,969M.
inputs.buyback_note: Actual financing outflows: FY2023 $688.7M, FY2024 $750.0M, FY2025 $500.0M, H1-2026 $603.6M. New $1B authorization (May 2026, Elliott cooperation agreement). A real repurchaser: the flat share count is being funded, not just a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.05 for large-cap medtech with a sensor/reimbursement concentration -> cost of equity ~9.5%. Debt is a 0.375% convert at ~6% of market cap, so WACC ~ cost of equity; 9.5% used in all scenarios (risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not in per-scenario WACCs).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost sits inside operating expenses and so inside EBITDA (no separate lease line). Finance-lease liability (~$59M) is included in total_debt; its principal is a financing flow and is not deducted from the projected flows. One treatment, not two.
inputs.nci_treatment: None; DexCom has no material non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted. Routing: DexCom is a US operating medical-device company (CGM sensors, razor/razorblade recurring revenue) -> SKILL.md row 1; no memory entry exists, so this is the first valuation. Base year FY2025 (revenue $4,662M); year 1 = FY2026, anchored to August 2026 guidance of $5.18-5.25B revenue (+11.9% at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA margin ~31.5-32% (pre-SBC, which is what ebitda_margin_path means here). Latest GAAP EBITDA + SBC: FY2025 28.4% (H1-25 25.0% depressed by scrap/freight/G7 quality costs, H2-25 31.4%), H1-2026 31.6%. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF $1,077.2M - SBC $159.6M - interest income $112.7M = $804.9M (17.3% of revenue); the component build gives ~16% in FY2026 because cash tax normalises from an abnormally low FY2025 ($94.4M paid on $1,088M pretax, 8.7%) and receivables/inventory absorb cash as revenue grows. Interest income is stripped because gross cash + securities ($1.95B) exceed the FCF base; the forward flows are EBITDA-based and exclude it by construction. Pending Nutrisense acquisition (announced June 2026, terms not material in the filings) is not modelled.

equity_bridge.note: LongTermInvestments, Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet (2026-06-30); non-operating, earn nothing inside EBITDA

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 revenue guidance midpoint ($5.215B vs $4.662B), decelerating; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (8.8% 3y / 12.1% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue (17.0% / 19.3%) and EPS (36.6% 3y) CAGRs. Book value is suppressed by ~$2.5B of buybacks FY2022-H1 2026 and the 2025 convert settlement, so it understates business growth; revenue and guidance are the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: EPS diluted split-adjusted (4:1 June 2022): FY2020 1.33, FY2022 0.82, FY2025 2.09. FY2020 EPS was inflated by a tax valuation-allowance release, which is why the 5y EPS CAGR (9.5%) is far below the 3y (36.6%). Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 ~157 (interest income untagged, ~0), FY2022 154.4, FY2025 804.9. Owner-FCF CAGRs exceed reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC has grown far slower than cash flow (3.4% of revenue in FY2025 vs 6.2% in FY2020) - the opposite of the dilution warning case. The FCF CAGRs start from a capex-heavy trough (Malaysia/Ireland plant build) and should not be extrapolated.

base.narrative_rationale: FY2026 at guidance (+11.9%, ~31.6% adj EBITDA). FY2028 margin dips 0.5pp and growth steps down for CMS competitive bidding (contracting 2027, pricing 2028). Margin then drifts to 33% on G7 15 Day / G8 cost-downs, below the bull case because Abbott keeps pricing pressure on Type 2. Capex eases from the plant-build 7-8% toward 6%, still above D&A. wc_capture negative: a manufacturer/distributor whose receivables + inventory exceed payables.

scenario_narratives.base: DexCom delivers FY2026 guidance and keeps double-digit growth into 2027 as the four-PBM coverage win opens the non-insulin Type 2 channel and international grows high-teens. CMS competitive bidding (contracts 2027, pricing 2028) takes a one-year bite out of U.S. DME reimbursement - growth slows to ~9.5% and margin gives back ~0.5pp in FY2028 - before G7 15 Day and G8 cost-downs lift adjusted EBITDA margin to ~33%. Abbott's Libre keeps the high-volume Type 2 and international segments price-competitive, so growth fades to ~3.5% by year 10 rather than compounding.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new management team (Leach/Sylvain) with Elliott on the board restores execution credibility: G7 15 Day reaches half the U.S. base by end-2026, G8 lands on schedule, and PBM coverage plus Stelo/Nutrisense convert a meaningful slice of the tens of millions of U.S. non-insulin Type 2 and prediabetic patients. CMS bidding proves manageable because DexCom's clinical data and pump-ecosystem integrations (Tandem, Insulet) protect its intensive-insulin share. Growth holds 11-13% for four years and adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 36% as sensor unit costs fall faster than price.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2024-2025 pattern of guidance misses repeats: scrap/freight overruns resurface in the G7 15 Day or G8 transition, and Abbott's cheaper, larger Libre franchise wins the non-insulin and international volume DexCom is now chasing. CMS competitive bidding sets a materially lower U.S. price from 2028, cutting growth to ~3% that year and resetting adjusted EBITDA margin to ~27-28% permanently. The biosensing pivot (Nutrisense, metabolic health) consumes capital without earning its cost. Growth settles at 4-5% and fades to 2.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because CMS competitive bidding is a dated, single-regulator catalyst hitting DexCom's most profitable channel and management has missed guidance twice in two years. Base 50% because FY2026 guidance has been raised twice and Q2 2026 beat. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (G8 on time, CMS benign, Type 2 conversion against Abbott).

valuation_philosophy.summary: DexCom is valued as a maturing razor/razorblade medtech: sensor revenue compounds with the installed base, and value rests on whether adjusted EBITDA margin can hold 31-33% through CMS competitive bidding and Abbott's price competition. SBC (including net-settlement withholding from 2026) is fully expensed; share count held flat, funded by real buybacks. Net cash is small relative to market cap, so the result is almost entirely an operating-margin and growth-duration call.
key_risks_to_valuation: CMS competitive bidding pricing from 2028 - the bear case's margin reset
Abbott Libre share gains in non-insulin Type 2 and international
Repeat of G7/G8 manufacturing scrap and freight overruns
Capital allocation in the biosensing pivot (Nutrisense and follow-on deals)
Terminal-value dependence: ~2/3 of value sits beyond year 10 on a 3% perpetuity
